cards.prompt: Which prompt gets the most useful first draft of a thank-you email to a client?

options.text: "Thank client Sam for our early finish. Under 80 words"
"Please write a lovely, professional thank-you email"
"Write a thank-you email, as long and detailed as you can"
"Write a thank-you email", with temperature turned right up

cards.explanation: Only the first gives the **goal**, the **context** (who Sam is, what they did) and the **format** (under 80 words). Politeness, length or temperature don't say who it's for.

cards.prompt: "Make a list of healthy snacks." What would improve this prompt **most**?

options.text: Saying who they're for and how many you want
Asking for lots of detail and plenty of examples
Asking it to include only snacks that are healthy
Turning the temperature up for more variety

cards.explanation: It has a goal but no context (for a lunchbox?) or format (how many?). More detail, repeating "healthy" or more temperature add neither.

cards.prompt: Sort these bits of prompts: the **goal**, the **context** or the **format**?

items.label: I'm 12 and it's for a science test
Here are my notes from class

cards.explanation: The **goal** is what to do; the **context** is who it's for and what you already have (your age, your notes); the **format** is the shape and length.

cards.prompt: A chatbot says "5 trays of 8 cupcakes is **45** cupcakes." Check it: how many are there really?
cards.explanation: 5 × 8 = **40**, not 45. A likely-looking number isn't always right, so check sums yourself.

cards.prompt: A chatbot says there are **about 50** kinds of penguin, with a link to a zoo's website.

steps.text: The link opens a real zoo page about penguins. What now?

choices.text: It's checked: the page is real
choices.consequence: A real page isn't proof. Read whether it says the same thing.

choices.text: Read the page to see what it says
choices.consequence: The page says there are about 18 kinds of penguin.
Asking the chatbot doesn't check anything.

steps.text: You tell it the page says about 18. It replies: "Sorry, you're right, it's 17." Which do you use?

choices.consequence: Right: go with the source you actually read, not the chatbot's new guess.
Its "fix" is just another guess. The page says 18.

cards.explanation: Open sources **and read them**, then go with what the source says. A chatbot's correction is just another prediction.

cards.prompt: A chatbot that can't search the web says a band's newest album came out "this year". Main risk?

options.text: It may have mixed the band up with another band
It can't handle dates, so its years are random guesses
It learned up to a certain date, so that may be old news
Its temperature was too high, so it picked a random year

cards.explanation: Without web search, a model only knows what it learned up to a certain date, so "this year" may be long out of date. Mix-ups happen, but that's the main risk.

cards.prompt: It's late, and you're stuck on one question in tomorrow's maths homework.

steps.text: You open a chatbot. What do you ask it?

choices.text: Explain the method on another example; I'll try mine
choices.consequence: It walks through a similar question, then you solve yours. You did the thinking.

choices.text: Give me the answer; I'll write it in my own words
choices.consequence: Rewriting its answer doesn't change who did the thinking, and you haven't learned the method.

choices.text: Give me the answer and working, so I can copy it neatly
choices.consequence: You'd hand in its work as yours, and still be stuck in the test.

cards.explanation: Using AI to **learn** (a method, then trying it yourself) is great. Getting it to **do the work**, even reworded, isn't, and many schools have rules about it.

cards.prompt: You're 14. A popular AI app's rules say **18 or older**, and your friends all use it. Best move?

options.text: Don't sign up yet: talk to a parent or carer
Ask an 18-year-old friend to share their account
Sign up, but never upload any photos of yourself
Sign up anyway: lots of people your age use it

cards.explanation: If an app says 18+, it isn't for you yet, whatever friends do, and borrowing an account still breaks the rules. **Check the rules and ask a parent or carer**.
